target_customer: Pharmaceutical and biotech companies running preclinical oncology drug efficacy and toxicity studies
problem: Standard cell culture and animal models poorly predict clinical drug response, so ineffective compounds advance too far.
business_model: Fee-for-service preclinical testing using patient-derived 3D tissue models
product_category: Preclinical 3D tissue models and contract research services

founders.name: Mukti Parikh
founders.background_notes: The only founder named on the YC page; no background given.

exit.reason: Merger of a Predictive Oncology subsidiary into zPREDICTA; announced December 1, 2021, with filings citing closing on November 24, 2021.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reconstructing patient-derived tissue with its extracellular environment in a plate format is a hard bioengineering problem, with clinical correlation data needed to be credible.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary protocols and trademarks (PD-3D, zPREDICTA filed 2016) protected the method, but contract research firms could build similar 3D assays.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Predictive Oncology acquired the company in late 2021 as a small subsidiary.

market_need_then: Not documented in sources dated near the batch; the company's own pitch cited correlation between platform efficacy data and clinical response.

branding.domain_note: Used zpredicta.com, which no longer resolves (DNS error) after the acquisition.

identity.logo: Not described in the sources found

brand_strength.rationale: A technical coined name aimed at scientists with no press about the brand found; trademarks were filed but sources show no brand pull.

outcome_analysis: zPREDICTA sold patient-derived 3D tissue models to drug developers from San Jose and joined YC in Summer 2015. It stayed tiny, with no public venture round found, and was merged into Predictive Oncology in November to December 2021. Filing figures report 2020 revenue of $563,288, so this was a small profitable lab-services business absorbed by a listed company.
notes: zpredicta.com does not resolve. The GlobeNewswire page returned 403 when fetched; the release date and the 8-K/A figures (2020 revenue $563,288) come from search result snippets. A directory reported a cash price of $10,015,941, while CB Insights says terms were undisclosed; unverified, so amount is null. Owler names Julia Kirshner as founder and CEO and Foundernest lists about $100K total funding; both are single aggregator entries, unverified and not used. Only Mukti Parikh is listed on the YC page. Competition left empty: search returned only recent articles on 3D tumor models. Acquisition date differs across sources: November 24 versus December 1, 2021.
